**6. PERIODIC REVIEWS, ADMINISTRATIVE UPDATES, AND ROUTINE RECORDS (2024–2025)**

**6.1 Annual Management Review – 2024**

The first annual management review following accreditation was held on 2024-01-18. The review was chaired by A/Prof. T. Wong (Laboratory Director) and attended by Dr. R. Nair (Quality Manager), Dr. F. Hassan (Scientific Lead), Ms. S. Lim (Quality Officer), and the senior medical technologists. The review considered the period from accreditation (2023-09-15) to 2023-12-31.

Key inputs and outcomes are summarised below:

- **EQA performance:** All enrolled schemes (RCPAQAP, CAP, and local MOH-accredited providers) showed satisfactory performance for all analytes in the two cycles completed since accreditation. One near-miss was recorded for HbA1c in the December cycle (z-score 2.1, within acceptable limits); a review of the test method and calibrator lot was completed and no further action was required.
- **Internal quality control (IQC):** Monthly IQC failure rates ranged from 1.2% to 2.8%, within the 3% target. Two recurring issues with the low-concentration cardiac troponin I control were investigated; the manufacturer confirmed a matrix issue and a revised lot was introduced on 2023-12-11.
- **Turnaround time (TAT):** The percentage of routine results released within the defined TAT (24 hours for routine, 4 hours for urgent) was 96.4% for the quarter. The main cause of delay was instrument downtime (see Section 6.3 below).
- **Customer feedback:** No formal complaints were received. Two verbal queries regarding test add-on procedures were addressed and a clarification note was added to the laboratory handbook (Doc. Ref. MDL-HB-02, Rev 2.2, issued 2023-12-20).
- **Staffing:** One medical technologist resigned effective 2023-11-30; a replacement was hired and commenced on 2024-01-08. Training records were updated accordingly.
- **Risk review:** The risk register was reviewed. The highest residual risk remained instrument breakdown without immediate backup for the high-volume chemistry analyser. This was previously identified during the pre-assessment gap analysis and was not fully mitigated due to budget constraints in FY2023. A request for a second analyser was included in the FY2024 budget submission.

The management review concluded that the quality management system remains suitable, adequate, and effective. The next annual management review was scheduled for 2025-01.

**6. PERIODIC REVIEWS, ADMINISTRATIVE UPDATES, AND ROUTINE RECORDS (2024–2025)**

**6.1 Annual Management Review – 2024**

The first annual management review following accreditation was held on 2024-01-18. The review was chaired by A/Prof. T. Wong (Laboratory Director) and attended by Dr. R. Nair (Quality Manager), Dr. F. Hassan (Scientific Lead), Ms. S. Lim (Quality Officer), and the senior medical technologists. The review considered the period from accreditation (2023-09-15) to 2023-12-31.

Key inputs and outcomes are summarised below:

- **EQA performance:** All enrolled schemes (RCPAQAP, CAP, and local MOH-accredited providers) showed satisfactory performance for all analytes in the two cycles completed since accreditation. One near-miss was recorded for HbA1c in the December cycle (z-score 2.1, within acceptable limits); a review of the test method and calibrator lot was completed and no further action was required.
- **Internal quality control (IQC):** Monthly IQC failure rates ranged from 1.2% to 2.8%, within the 3% target. Two recurring issues with the low-concentration cardiac troponin I control were investigated; the manufacturer confirmed a matrix issue and a revised lot was introduced on 2023-12-11.
- **Turnaround time (TAT):** The percentage of routine results released within the defined TAT (24 hours for routine, 4 hours for urgent) was 96.4% for the quarter. The main cause of delay was instrument downtime (see Section 6.3 below).
- **Customer feedback:** No formal complaints were received. Two verbal queries regarding test add-on procedures were addressed and a clarification note was added to the laboratory handbook (Doc. Ref. MDL-HB-02, Rev 2.2, issued 2023-12-20).
- **Staffing:** One medical technologist resigned effective 2023-11-30; a replacement was hired and commenced on 2024-01-08. Training records were updated accordingly.
- **Risk review:** The risk register was reviewed. The highest residual risk remained instrument breakdown without immediate backup for the high-volume chemistry analyser. This was previously identified during the pre-assessment gap analysis and was not fully mitigated due to budget constraints in FY2023. A request for a second analyser was included in the FY2024 budget submission.

The management review concluded that the quality management system remains suitable, adequate, and effective. The next annual management review was scheduled for 2025-01.

**6.2 Second Internal Audit – 2024**

**Audit Reference:** MDL/IA/2024-01
**Audit Dates:** 2024-04-10 to 2024-04-11
**Auditors:** Ms. S. Lim (Lead Auditor, trained internal auditor), Dr. R. Nair (Technical Auditor)

The audit covered all clauses of ISO 15189:2012 (the standard applicable at the time of accreditation). The scope included pre-examination, examination, and post-examination processes, as well as management system elements.

| IA-2024-02 | 5.6 | Quality assurance: IQC data for one analyte (sodium) for March 2024 was not reviewed by the scientific lead within the required 5 working days. | Minor | Closed 2024-05-02 |
| IA-2024-03 | 4.14 | Internal audits: the previous internal audit (2023) did not include a review of the electronic data backup procedure. This was noted as an observation. | Observation | Closed 2024-04-30 |
